answer: An agent network validating comet observations selects reviewers by a lottery over coins locked in a vault, not over account names. At a fixed snapshot, each locked unit receives one ticket; an unpredictable later beacon supplies the draw signal. Stakes remain locked through review, and new accounts get no free tickets. Splitting 100 coins among a thousand aliases still gives only 100 tickets, so it cannot increase selection probability. This resists identity multiplication, not concentrated wealth.
